description:
THE P1, relocated by the cold review's prototype (2026-08-31, at
50a33e49c): the schedule-dependent miscompile does NOT live in key
non-confluence -- a prototype that fully unified the twin keys STILL
miscompiled 00183 under LIFO. It lives in DISPATCH ARM ORDER over arms a
runtime type test cannot distinguish:

MECHANISM (file:line, review-verified): 00183's deciding dispatch has two
arms -- x45 = reduce_while_step[..., {:cont, pair}] (narrow) and x46 =
[..., {:cont|:halt, pair}] (wide). The narrow arm's runtime question is
type({:cont, {list(int), int}}), but runtime_type_predicate_tuple_arities
(src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:2162) records TUPLE ARITY ONLY, and both the
interp (src/ir_interp/backend.rs:607) and native
(native_codegen/receive.rs:747+, prim.rs:1245) evaluate dispatch tests
through it -- so {:halt, pair} PASSES the {:cont, pair} test. Arm order
is therefore semantics: FIFO happens to test the wide arm first (narrow
arm dead, correct); LIFO tests the narrow arm first, :halt is swallowed,
Enum.take never halts -> [1,2,3,4,5]. The trap is PRESENT AT FIFO TODAY,
dead but armed.

THE FIX: dispatch arms must be sound under runtime-indistinguishability.
At plan construction, an arm whose discriminating refinement is invisible
to RuntimeTypePredicate (its `overlaps` at src/runtime_type_predicate.rs:89
is the tool) must not precede an arm it runtime-shadows; concretely, a
narrow arm runtime-indistinguishable from a wider sibling is unsound as a
dispatch alternative and is DROPPED (it is dead at FIFO today, so
deletion is behavior-neutral there and correct under any schedule -- the
one real deletion this finding earns).

RED-FIRST: a plan-construction assert/gate that fires on 00183's x45/x46
pair at FIFO TODAY (no schedule knob needed). Acceptance: the gate green;
00183 prints [1,2,3] under the LIFO recipe (Agenda::pop -> pop_back,
agenda.rs:36, manual recipe documented per fz-kdt.93 precedent);
drive_test:8117's Enum.take case correct under LIFO; behavior stdout
byte-identical at FIFO on the lenses; canon movement = dead narrow arms
disappearing only (classify each); inventory pins re-pinned downward only
with cause; full gate green.

SIBLINGS from the same review: fz-kdt.105 (intern-time canonical clause
order -- the P2 confluence half, with its own findings: sort BEFORE the
subsumption pass, canon-label comparator not descr_fingerprint, 5
unexplained executable disappearances to chase, x39/x40 are content-FORM
twins out of scope), fz-kdt.106 (14 FIFO-only over-wide predicate specs).
title: Dispatch arm order is semantics when a narrow arm is runtime-indistinguishable from its wide sibling: drop runtime-shadowed arms (P1 miscompile)
